source_name: Nexi Group — press releases / media relations archive
why_relevant: Nexi (post SIA + Nets consolidation) is a direct competitor/supplier in the SI payments vendor layer and owns a Slovenian operating entity. Group press releases are where CEE go-lives, acquiring wins and bank partnerships surface first.

source_name: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. — company records (Bizi / Companywall / eBonitete)
why_relevant: Slovenian business registers expose the local processing entity's revenue (~EUR 23.8m 2024), headcount, directors, owner (Nexi Croatia) and — crucially — the chain of prior names (Intesa Sanpaolo Card → Nets CEE → Nexi Slovenija), which reconstructs the ownership history of SI card processing capacity without any vendor disclosure.

source_name: AJPES — Slovenian business register and annual reports (primary registry)
why_relevant: Primary official source behind all SI company aggregators: legal entity data, ownership, and filed annual reports for payments vendors (Bankart, Nexi Slovenija, Paywiser, Cetis and similar). Annual reports often name major system investments and contracts.

source_name: European Payments Council — 'Instant payment environment in Slovenia' insight + SCT Inst participant register
why_relevant: Scheme-level authority describing the SI instant-payment environment (BIPS, Flik, adherence). EPC also publishes scheme adherence registers, which identify which SI PSPs are live on SCT Inst and therefore which have completed a platform implementation.

source_name: NLB Group — Bankart shareholding/subsidiary pages
why_relevant: Bank-side disclosure of ownership in the national processor. Bank group reports and subsidiary pages are an independent check on processor ownership structure and strategy, and NLB's regional footprint hints at cross-border processing consolidation.

source_name: NLB — POS terminal / card & Flik acceptance pages and merchant ordering portal
why_relevant: Acquirer-facing product pages reveal terminal estates, accepted schemes, Flik acceptance and digital onboarding stacks (e.g. Rekono digital identity in the ordering flow) — indirect evidence of which acceptance and identity vendors sit behind the largest SI acquirer.

source_name: Gorenjska banka / OTP banka / Pošta Slovenije — card & Flik acceptance and general terms documents
source_subtype: bank product page + terms & conditions PDFs
why_relevant: Mid-tier acquirers' merchant pages and 'splošni pogoji' PDFs name the processing chain, gateway, scheme set and sometimes the technical provider — a reliable indirect route to who processes for banks that never issue press releases.

source_name: Paywiser d.o.o. — EMI with issuing/acquiring processing stack (corporate site + EMI profile)
why_relevant: Bank of Slovenia-licensed e-money institution, PCI DSS certified for card issuing and processing, EEA-passported. Represents the non-bank issuing/processing layer in SI and is a candidate buyer or competitor for issuing platforms.

source_name: OpenWay Group — Way4 platform site and customer/reference pages
why_relevant: Global issuing/acquiring/switch platform vendor active across CEE; its reference and migration pages are where a Slovenian processor win would be announced. Treat as a watch-list vendor site rather than a confirmed SI supplier — no SI reference was found in this pass.

source_name: Visa Partner Directory (Visa Ready certified issuer processors)
why_relevant: Scheme-maintained directory of certified issuer processors and technology partners; filtering by geography surfaces which processors are scheme-certified to serve SI issuers — a structured alternative to scattered press releases.

source_name: Mastercard — licensing guide and gateway/partner certification pages
why_relevant: Defines membership/certification categories and lists certified gateway and processing partners; the mechanism by which processor certifications become publicly announceable, and a lookup route from scheme side into national vendor stacks.

source_name: Portal javnih naročil / eNaročanje (Slovenian public procurement portal)
why_relevant: Tender notices and awards from public-sector bodies and state-influenced entities (Pošta Slovenije, public bodies procuring card/terminal services) name suppliers, contract values and technical requirements — the highest-fidelity public trace of payments-vendor selection where a public buyer is involved.

source_name: HRC d.o.o. — Hibis core banking vendor (SI/HR banks and savings banks)
why_relevant: One of the largest suppliers of banking software to SI and HR banks/savings banks with its own Hibis core platform. Relevant to this cell as the integration counterparty for payments/card modules at smaller SI institutions, and as a route to identify which banks outsource payments components.

source_name: SRC d.o.o. — PSD2/open banking platform case study
why_relevant: Slovenian systems integrator publishing a named PSD2 platform case study for banks — an example of the local integrator layer adjacent to payments (API/open-banking gateways), and a template for the kind of case-study content SI IT firms publish about bank projects.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenia — Flik product and instant-payment pages
why_relevant: Issuer-side view of the Flik/instant-payment rollout at a foreign-owned SI bank; useful for mapping which banks are live on which scheme features and, historically, this group's link to the card-processing entity that became Nexi Slovenija.

source_name: ivarnost.si — sector article profiling Bankart as leading SI payments solution provider
why_relevant: Slovenian security/technology outlet publishing vendor profiles that summarise Bankart's service portfolio and direction (open banking, instant payments, mobile, e-identity). Useful for narrative and strategy signals not present in corporate pages.

source_name: poslovni.si — SI business news covering interbank payment operations and infrastructure events
why_relevant: Local business media report scheduled infrastructure events (migration windows, interbank payment stoppages) that reveal when core payment platforms are being changed or upgraded — an operational-calendar signal rarely announced by vendors.

source_name: Cetis d.d. / Cetis Identity — card and secure document personalisation
why_relevant: Slovenian secure-document and card personalisation manufacturer; named in secondary sources alongside Bankart and Euronet as an acquiring/processing-adjacent provider. Relevant as the physical card issuance/personalisation tier of the SI payments vendor stack. Card-payment role not directly confirmed in this pass (tachograph/ID card evidence dominates).

source_name: Dnevi slovenske informatike (DSI) – sponsors page
why_relevant: DSI is Slovenia's flagship informatics conference; its tiered sponsor list (general/diamond/gold/silver/bronze/media) is a paid, dated declaration of which IT vendors are courting Slovenian enterprise and public-sector buyers, including banks. Observed tiers in 2026 include NIL d.o.o. (general), Lek (HackathON diamond), Microsoft (gold), 3 GEN, Bplanet, Comtrade, DELL, Endava (silver).

source_name: Dnevi slovenske informatike – programme and speakers (govorci)
why_relevant: Agenda and speaker list names vendor speakers alongside bank/public-sector executives; 2026 tracks include AI, digital public services, cybersecurity, data management. Speaker affiliation is a leading indicator of vendor-bank relationships before deals are announced.

source_name: Slovensko društvo Informatika (SDI) – event organiser page
why_relevant: SDI organises DSI and awards; its events section is the upstream announcement channel for editions, calls for papers, and award ceremonies, useful for discovering new event instances and sub-events (hackathon sponsors, award categories).

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) – Bančna konferenca
why_relevant: The central annual Slovenian banking conference (Brdo pri Kranju; 2026 edition 3 June, theme on geopolitics, digitalisation and 'new' sovereignty). Panel line-ups name Bank of Slovenia vice-governors, KDD IT directors and bank executives — the exact buyer population vendors target — and any commercial partners of the event.

source_name: ZBS terminski plan (annual event/training calendar)
why_relevant: Forward calendar of every ZBS conference, posvetovanje and training for the year — the single best pointer for scheduling collection of Slovenian banking events, including the card-business consultation and treasurer/back-office consultations where payments vendors present.

source_name: ZBS posvetovanje o kartičnem poslovanju (card business consultation)
why_relevant: Annual consultation aimed at leading and expert staff in card business at banks, savings banks and other institutions. This is the narrowest, highest-signal Slovenian gathering for cards/payments vendors; its agenda names who is invited to speak about card innovations and trends.

source_name: Bančni vestnik (ZBS journal) – conference proceedings and special issues
why_relevant: The only Slovenian monthly journal for money and banking (since 1951, EconLit-indexed). Special/English issues frequently package conference contributions, and article authorship reveals which vendors and consultancies get platformed by ZBS. Useful as the written residue of events whose agendas are otherwise ephemeral.

source_name: ZBS letno poročilo (annual report) – event and working-group record
why_relevant: Retrospective, dated record of which conferences, consultations and working groups ZBS actually ran, with counts and themes — lets a collector reconstruct historical event series that no longer have live pages.

source_name: Money Motion (Zagreb) – sponsors page
why_relevant: The dominant regional (Adriatic/SEE) fintech and payments conference, co-founded by ASEE and Monri; sponsors observed include Nexi, Mastercard, OTP Bank, Monri, ASEE, Payten. Slovenian banks and vendors attend, and the sponsor tiering is the clearest paid signal of regional payments-vendor intent affecting the SI market.
